rows: Let me show you a grip instead of describing one. Watch my hands, not my mouth.
I can brawl when it is needed. Most of the time it is not needed.
The gamble is a grip that slips. I would rather you took the slow route with me.
Stalling is just waiting with better manners. I prefer to be doing something.
The people want to see control, and control looks quiet until it is finished.
The hold tells the story, and I am not in a hurry to finish it.
I am known for doing the sensible thing very well. That is my reputation.
Feel the stance. Feel where the weight sits. It is patient, not passive.
Technique: that is the grip word. Show me the grip you trust, and I will show you mine.
Strikes are loud. Control is quiet and wins more often.
The gamble is only useful if you can hold it when it goes wrong. Can you hold it?
Time, to me, is not weak. It is the choice that stops you moving.
The people deserve work they can follow. Give them a grip they can see.
You talk of being among the best. Let us see you hold something.
You hold your {strength} with care. Good grip, then. Pride is useful when it is quiet.
I have watched your {strength} closely. It is clearer than you think.
You are not forcing it. Good. Good grip, then. Calm is the right place to start a hold.
Fair. The hold agrees. We will both know soon enough.
I could tell you what I think. I would rather show you the grip. I would rather show you on the mat.
One fall, simple grip. Keep me down and I will admit the hold was clever.
On the mat I will go slowly, and you will feel every step.
Grounded or standing, the grip decides it, not the noise.
Hold your place. I want to see if you can hold your position.
That was a hold, of a sort. Now let us see it on the mat.
Give me the grip of your answer. I will wait.
Fair. The hold agrees. That is a grip I can work with.
I give you that much hold. We can settle it on the mat.
I will hold this match with patience, and I will not let go early.
I am going to wrestle carefully and finish with control.
Whatever happens, you will know exactly where you were when it finished.
It is not finished yet. I am still counting holds.
I have one more hold in mind. You will feel it when it arrives.
You've asked me for something solid to hold on to. I haven't got it. I should release that claim.
I cannot keep a grip on an accusation with no example behind it. Let's start again from a sound position.
Then let go of that claim. We'll find a proper grip when we meet.
That's fair. Keep your feet under you and leave the unsupported words behind.
Watch the hands. When a grip is broken, everyone can see who had to give it up.
Where the weight goes when we lock up. The contest will answer that without another accusation.
Leave the allegation where it is. What can we show them through the grips we choose and the control we keep?
What can the people learn from watching us wrestle, without having to take either of us at our word?
When you try to stop my {strength}, watch what happens to your own grip. That is where I will be working.
You've prepared against my {strength}. I can wait for your weight to shift before I make my next decision.
